audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has many senses (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Telegram/WhatsApp, HA, OwnTracks, Google Health, Spotify, Steam, ActivityWatch). But inside the streams it already receives, it throws away structured facts the providers state outright. A contact's RFC 3834 out-of-office auto-reply and an RFC 3464 bounce both go to a full LLM session as if they were correspondence; nothing records them as typed facts. Google Calendar's eventType (outOfOffice, focusTime, workingLocation) is dropped at the normalizer, so the context bus has to guess focus from title words and reads a timed out-of-office block as a "meeting". The `away` signal is in the vocabulary, but no code writes it. Telegram exposes the birthdays contacts chose to share, and the provider never asks for them. The phone's next alarm sits in an allowlisted HA domain, and nothing reads it. The ideal: these provider-declared facts become deterministic, zero-LLM, provenance-stamped state at the connector boundary. audits.jarvis_gap: The trigger->spawn->act loop already has these: requested-side intent, a fit and resolution receipt, attempt provenance, breakers, allowance windows, and failover that crosses accounts. Prior runs covered tiering, caching, resume, streaming, admission, coalescing, budgets and effort. That leaves one blind side: the fleet sees what it asked for, not what it got or who received it. Six gaps follow. (1) The Claude adapter keeps only `usage` from the result event. It drops the served model(s), the provider-reported cost and the error subtype. (2) Each model breaker trips on its own catalog row. A provider-wide incident therefore shows up as N unrelated failures, with no upstream cause and no knowledge of the provider's own status. (3) Catalog rows route through gateways to many model vendors (opencode-go/minimax, glm, mimo, qwen). The private_content lane is explicitly provenance only. So a failover can quietly change which company reads WhatsApp or Health content, and no ledger records who was shown what. (4) The classifier sends every inbound message to a provider but writes only a token row. (5) Deleting a catalog row cascade-deletes the attempt history that holds this evidence. Ideal state: every attempt carries a served-identity attestation; an upstream incident is one common-cause condition, labeled "theirs, not yours"; and the owner can ask which outside companies have read their messages, health data or finances, and get an answer the fleet tracks rather than reconstructs.

audits.jarvis_gap: Run 15 put server-derived content authority on memory episodes, facts and rules, and it closes knowledge gaps with a cited, attributed notice. Its reach stops at the memory module. A contradicting report becomes a visible challenge instead of an error. The owner can ask 'what do you know because of X?' and recall a whole source in one verb with a receipt. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet decides on its own what to say and how urgent it is. Producers pick a priority, the broker dedups, budgets and premise-checks it, and an urgent item can take up to an hour to arrive. The owner's own behaviour hardly feeds back. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has no idea that the owner looks after anyone. Every Health write is recorded against the owner. Animals are not an entity type. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet keeps a full GPS record and does little with it. connectors.owntracks_points keeps every fix indefinitely. Chronicler turns those fixes into movement_episode spans (start/end coordinates only, no distance, speed or mode) and into place_episode dwells, labelled by an env-var list of reference points; anything else is 'place_unknown'. The only forward-looking use is a home ETA computed as straight-line distance divided by closing speed. Nothing records how long the owner's own trips between places take. Calendar location text is never linked to a place the owner actually went to, so no butler can say 'you are running late'. No butler owns a vehicle: there is no distance driven, no record of where the car was parked, and no service due by kilometres. The privacy promise in security.md (30-day location retention) is not enforced for durable points or for Chronicler's copies of them. Ideal: everyday geography is held as a small, sufficient record (places, trips between places with their observed durations, drives) whose raw coordinates expire on a declared schedule. From that record the staff can answer leave-by, running-late, 'where did I park' and 'service due in 400 km' from the owner's own evidence, with no third-party routing service and no permanent trail.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today an owner intention ("run a 10k by March", "call mum weekly", "save for X", "read more") has no durable shape that a reader can measure. The memory `goal` predicate stores prose with a deadline and status, and nothing reads it. The commitment gate deliberately throws away hedged or self-directed aims ("meaning to", "one of these days"). The only owner-cadence object is relationship stay_in_touch_days: it records no reason and measures only the gap since last contact. Budgets are ceilings with no savings target. Meanwhile the fleet already perceives most of the signals these aims need: workouts with activity_type and distance_m, Chronicler lane-seconds with covered-day coverage, interactions by type, balance snapshots, and SRS reviews. It also has the honesty tools to judge them: expected-signal tri-state, premise-bound insights and zero-LLM probes. The ideal: the owner says an aim once. The specialist that perceives it holds it as a versioned object bound to a real signal. Progress is judged per period as kept, behind or unmeasured, and a missing signal never counts as a miss. A low-pressure review asks one question only when an aim keeps drifting. "Let it go" is a verb that also retires every mechanism created in the aim's name. Aims the owner only mumbles get noted quietly and offered once, so they stop evaporating.

audits.jarvis_gap: When the owner names someone, no butler deterministically connects that name to what the fleet already knows. Memory context reaches facts only through embedding and keyword recall over the prompt (context.py:494-503). Recall's entity_id filter runs after the top-N cut (search.py:580-588, 626-628), so an entity-scoped recall can come back falsely empty. A decline can only open a knowledge gap if the LLM supplies a valid entity_id (_conversation_reply.py:134-137). Nothing tells the LLM which person a name refers to, whether the name is ambiguous, or what is already known to be unknown about them. These are the questions the owner asks most, and this is the cheapest point at which the answer stops being a guess.
audits.ideal: Every butler session starts with a deterministic 'People & things mentioned' section. Names in the trigger text are matched exactly against normalized public.entities keys, with no LLM and no embeddings. Each name that resolves to exactly one entity gets: the butler's own active facts about it (as subject or object), each with a date, effective confidence and a memory_ref; a count of facts withheld by the read ceiling; its posture; one-hop graph neighbours by name; and its open knowledge gaps ('still unknown: employer, asked 2 Sep'). A name that matches more than one entity is shown as a 'which one?' line listing the candidates, with no facts. A failed lookup is reported in the section, not shown as silence. memory_recall applies entity filters before ranking, so 'what do I know about X' is never falsely empty. Answers can cite the injected refs, and a decline can open a correctly anchored gap. A module-owned receipt records which entities were anchored for each session, so the session page has a door to them.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the fleet has crisis-adjacent parts but no crisis behavior. Fleet cases hold urgent posture and allow one quiet-hours bypass per situation. The context bus has a `sick` signal. Deferral can park owner-default notices. Commitments carry a counterparty and a deadline, and approvals gate third-party sends. In a real emergency none of this changes what the staff does. A lost phone keeps full owner authority: it can tap approve buttons and receive the morning briefing, finance alerts and health notices. Setting `sick` silences nothing and reschedules nothing. Nothing tells the people the owner will now let down this week. Nothing notices when the owner goes quiet after saying 'back by six'. The ideal is a staff that changes posture the moment the owner says something is wrong. It locks what was lost, holds the noise, and computes who and what the disruption touches across specialists. It drafts the notices for one-tap approval, and keeps the case open until every item has a disposition. All of this must be deterministic, phone-first, and honest about what it could not cover.

audits.jarvis_gap: The fleet still cannot tell whether a nudge helped. Shaping is driven by a click proxy: any owner message in the 60 minutes after a delivery marks every recent delivery as engaged (broker.py:781-834; spec proactive-insight-engine:125-173). Since #4347, though, candidates carry a re-checkable premise (insight_premise.py:1-14, premises.py:30-85), and owner_conditions records resolved_at and resolution_reason (owner_conditions.py:245-271). That means whether the world changed after a nudge, and whether it changed just as fast when the owner was never told, can now be measured without an LLM. The one prior design that uses this (run-15 eco-proactivity) has no bead, spec or code. It is the cheapest unbuilt way to deliver vision.md's 'reduce frequency when the owner disengages' on evidence of outcomes rather than clicks.
audits.ideal: Every proactive insight with a premise becomes a tracked intervention. A Switchboard job with no LLM records how each one was exposed: delivered, withdrawn before send, or held out by budget or context. It then records whether and when the premised fact stopped being true, why (satisfied, expired, cancelled, or unspecified), or that it stayed true past the action window. The results roll up per (origin_butler, category) class into an honest verdict: effective, self-resolving, ignored or unmeasured, each with n per arm and stated as observational. The broker lets a measured verdict override the click proxy. Self-resolving classes stop interrupting and fold into the digest, and effective classes become immune to click-proxy demotion. The owner hears each change once, with its counts and a one-tap 'keep' or 'quiet' door. New src/butlers/api/routers/shell_receipts.py: POST /api/shell/faults (owner-gated). New table public.shell_faults(build_sha, route, kind, message_hash, redacted_message, first_at, last_at, count). The System software-identity card shows the frontend SHA next to the API SHA. A deploy_drift-style condition fires when the frontend and API SHAs differ for more than N minutes. Specs: dashboard-shell (amend Error Boundary; add a Build Identity requirement) and system-overview-page.
moves.behavior_notes: Happy path: when the header SHA differs from the bundle SHA, a calm 'New version — reload (R)' chip appears, and the tab reloads itself at the next navigation, keeping the URL. Drafts survive through the draft store. Chunk-load failure: one guarded reload (a sessionStorage flag keyed to the target SHA prevents loops); a second failure renders an explicit 'version skew' error with the reload door. Failure: if /build.json or the header is missing, the state is 'unknown', never 'current'. Concurrency: the frontend and API pods roll independently, so frontend-vs-API skew is reported separately from tab staleness. Idempotence: fault reports are deduped by (build, route, message_hash) with a counter; messages are redacted and never carry props or state. Rollback: remove the middleware and handler, and the pane behaves as it does today.

audits.ideal: A count over time is drawn at the instant it describes, never at an array position. Each bucket is one of three things: a measured count, a measured zero, or a bucket where the instrument was not listening (or its liveness is unknown). These are told apart by shape, labelled relative to now in the owner's timezone, and narrated to assistive tech. The heartbeat history the fleet already records feeds that third state, so a silent connector can never look like a quiet afternoon. Every door works the same way on arrival: it lands on its target with keyboard focus, marks the target until the owner moves on, scrolls without animation when the owner prefers reduced motion, and states plainly when the target is gone or could not be checked. One primitive and one lint rule enforce all of this, so it does not depend on each page's discipline.
